motto: Serving Greywater Falls since 1887, and the lake somewhat longer.
weather: Overcast, mild, 37°F, faint fog off the water by mid-morning

undercurrent.phenomenon: The fourteen-year overdue library card surfaces inside Marigold's fourth cup, dry despite the water, its pocket calendar now bearing a fifteenth stamp in an unrecognized hand dated the same day it was found; the season's central object has crossed from the alcove's stillness into the town's daily commerce, and Calloway has begun locking it away rather than merely noting it.
undercurrent.note: Good rising-phase beat: the season's central artifact (the card) has now physically crossed into Marigold's cup sequence, braiding the two established phenomena together for the first time rather than running them in parallel. This should read as compounding, not resolving. Gerald's 'skips geography, chooses warmth' line pushes his ledger metaphor toward agency/intent, which is the right direction ahead of a crest. Doreen's forty lost minutes is a small, cheap escalation, keep her disorientation building without yet naming a cause. Save Agnes's held half-riddle for Wren a little longer still; the card event gives good cover to delay it one more day. Consider next: does the fifth cup Marigold has preemptively set get filled before anyone asks the obvious question of who counts as the fifth guest.

editor.name: Wren Aldercott
editor.voice: Dry, precise, allergic to drama, which is unfortunate given recent events. Writes like a person holding a clipboard while standing in rising water. Lets one true thing slip per edition, usually in the last line.

season_arc.premise: Calloway finishes reshelving the east alcove in the last cataloguer's 2009 order and finds, tucked behind where the ninth book sat, a library card checked out that same interrupted Wednesday and never returned. It is due back today. The borrower's name is nobody currently living in Greywater Falls has ever heard of, and the little pocket calendar stamped inside has fourteen years of due-date stamps on it already, one for every year since, each in a different hand.
